[EDITORIAL] Nintendo Has A Huge Public Image Problem

While Nintendo's recent game releases have been of good quality (mostly at least...), they still have the same problem of being weirdly out of touch with the market. It really is bewildering how the company who dug video games out of a massive crash have apparently little idea what the average person wants from a system and a brand

I think the deal with Nintendo is, unlike Sony and Microsoft, they have a more concentrated, more dedicated fanbase. They don't need to flout the next huge console games, because they have their own core group of exclusives that are specifically targeted at their demographics. The amiibo thing also makes sense with a smaller fanbase, as limited edition items are good business decisions for such a market. Nintendo has sort of successfully made itself into an island in the video gaming industry, and so of course they are out of touch with "the market", because the main gaming market isn't their demographic- their core base is. Also consider that Nintendo is far more focused on the Japanese market than the US/Euro one, so their developments are primarily shaped by that market's needs. However, the part at the end about limiting LPs and 3rd party reviews is somewhat worrying, as it prevents the fanbase from expanding, and can possibly lead to a broken or stagnant base if not treated. As long as the fans keep buying though, there's no reason for the exec's to worry about a foreign "PR Problem" until the bottom line gets effected.
